fixes.explanation: Herod tells his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him." (Matthew 14:2). Herod hears the reports and lands on a conclusion faster than anybody reading half a group chat. Notice he's the one connecting the dots here, and he lands on John.

John had been telling Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have her." (Matthew 14:4). Herodias was Herod's brother Philip's wife, and John said it to Herod himself. Matthew tells us Herod arrested him, bound him and put him in prison on account of her.
The text says the opposite. The daughter of Herodias danced before them "…and pleased Herod" (Matthew 14:6). Herod was pleased, and that matters for what happens next.

That's right, it's false. Matthew says the daughter of Herodias danced before them "…and pleased Herod" (Matthew 14:6). The next verse shows how much, because he promises with an oath to give her whatever she asks (Matthew 14:7). It was his birthday, and he made a big promise.

Matthew says she was "Prompted by her mother…" (Matthew 14:8). So her mother is the one who prompted her before the girl tells Herod what she wants. The text tells us who prompted her, and that's all it tells us. It doesn't say how or what was said between them.

It's true, not false. Matthew says the girl was "Prompted by her mother…" (Matthew 14:8). Her mother is the one who prompted her before she answers Herod. The text gives us the mother's part, and it doesn't say more than that.
